component LibraryMeetDeclarations
import List.{...}
import Random.{...}
export Executable

inOrder(g: Generator[\ZZ32\]): String = do
    s: String := ""
    for x <- seq(g) do s := s || x || "," end
    s
end

run() = do
    j = Just[\ZZ32\](3)
    n = Nothing[\ZZ32\]
    m: Maybe[\ZZ32\] = j
    assert(j.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x + 1).asString, "Just(4)", "Just(3) mapped by adding one is Just(4)")
    assert(m.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x + 1).asString, "Just(4)", "a Maybe holding 3 mapped by adding one is Just(4)")
    assert(n.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x + 1).asString, "Nothing", "Nothing mapped is Nothing")
    assert(j.ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => i + x + 10).asString, "Just(13)", "Just(3) mapped with its index 0 is Just(13)")
    assert(m.ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => i + x + 10).asString, "Just(13)", "a Maybe holding 3 mapped with its index 0 is Just(13)")
    assert(n.ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => i + x + 10).asString, "Nothing", "Nothing mapped with its index is Nothing")

    a = array[\ZZ32\](3).fill(7)
    c = a.copy()
    c[1] := 9
    assert(a[1], 7, "writing to an array's copy leaves the array unchanged")
    assert(c[1], 9, "an array's copy takes the write")

    assert(MaxReduction[\ZZ32\].lift(3).asString, "Just(3)", "an associative reduction lifts its operand into Just")
    assert(LessThan CMP LessThan, EqualTo, "LessThan CMP LessThan is EqualTo")
    assert(GreaterThan CMP GreaterThan, EqualTo, "GreaterThan CMP GreaterThan is EqualTo")
    assert(LexicographicReduction.isLeftZero(LessThan), false, "today's value: the lexicographic reduction answers its inherited isLeftZero for a total comparison")
    assert(BIG MAX[x <- 0#4] x, 3, "BIG MAX over 0#4 is 3, one element")

    nested = (0#3).nest[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32): Generator[\ZZ32\] => (10 i)#2)
    assert(inOrder(seq(nested)), "0,1,10,11,20,21,", "seq of a nested generator generates the inner elements in order")
    assert(seq((0#2).cross[\ZZ32\](0#2)).asString, "seq(seq(0,1).cross(seq(0,1)))", "seq of a pair generator is the sequential pair of the two sequential generators")

    kept = (0#6).filter(fn (x: ZZ32): Boolean => x > 1)
    assert(inOrder(kept.filter(fn (x: ZZ32): Boolean => x < 5)), "2,3,4,", "a filter generator filtered again keeps the elements both predicates keep")
    mappedIndexed = (0#3).map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x + 1)
    twice = mappedIndexed.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => 10 x)
    assert(inOrder(twice), "10,20,30,", "an indexed generator mapped twice applies both functions in order")
    assert(twice[1], 20, "an indexed generator mapped twice is still indexed")
    mapped = kept.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x + 1)
    assert(inOrder(mapped.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => 10 x)), "30,40,50,60,", "a mapped generator mapped again composes the two functions")

    increasing = relationalPredicate[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32, y: ZZ32): Boolean => x < y)
    rising = increasing(0#3)
    assert(rising.holds, true, "0, 1, 2 is increasing")
    assert(rising.relation()(1, 2), true, "the relation of an increasing predicate holds of 1 and 2")
    assert(inOrder(rising.target()), "0,1,2,", "a relational predicate's target is the generator it was applied to")
    assert(increasing(<|[\ZZ32\] 2, 1|>).holds, false, "2, 1 is not increasing")

    empty = ""
    flat = "abc"
    assert(empty.split().asString, "Nothing", "the empty string splits into no pieces")
    assert(empty.splitWithOffsets().asString, "Nothing", "the empty string splits into no pieces with offsets")
    assert(flat.split().asString, "Nothing", "a flat string answers no subdivision")

# harness-one.sh <scratch-dir> <file.fss>... : rung C's harness-one.sh (explorations/compile-ladder/
# rung-interp-coercion/, itself rung I's shape): the testSystem harness (SystemJUTest, the class build.xml's
# testSystem shards run) over a directory holding only the named test files, with the JVM settings of
# build.xml's systemShard macro and a private cache. Run from FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh.
set -u
S=${1:?scratch dir} ; shift
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:?}
rm -rf "$S" ; mkdir -p "$S/tests" "$S/caches" "$S/tmp"
printf '\0\0\0\0' > "$S/caches/global.map"
for f in "$@" ; do cp "$f" "$S/tests/" ; done
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
echo "# harness-one $(date -u +%FT%TZ); tree $(git -C "$FH" rev-parse --short HEAD); nproc=$(nproc); load $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=1"
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress" && FORTRESS_THREADS=1 FORTRESS_JUNIT_VERBOSE=1 FORTRESS_CACHES="$S/caches" \
  java -Xmx768m -Xss32m -Djava.io.tmpdir="$S/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$S/caches" -Dtests="$S/tests" \
       -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.tests.unit_tests.SystemJUTest 2>&1 | grep -v '^\s*at ' | sed "s#$FH/##g"
echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
rm -rf "$S"

content.content:
component AssertRung4
export Executable

(*) Rung 4 of the compile-path ladder: the comparing forms of assert and deny.
(*) The interpreter declares assert(x:Any, y:Any, failMsg:Any...) and the
(*) matching deny at Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:234 and :236 (implementation
(*) Library/FortressLibrary.fss:296 and :306).  The compiler world declares
(*) only assert(Boolean) and assert(Boolean, String) at
(*) Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:35-36; the comparing form sits commented out at
(*) Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:89-95, so every compilation that writes
(*) assert(x, y) or assert(x, y, msg) stops at typecheck with
(*) "Could not check call to function assert".
(*)
(*) The shapes exercised here are the shapes the blocked programs call, read
(*) off explorations/compile-ladder/raw/tests/: (ZZ32, ZZ32) with an IntLiteral
(*) on either side, (ZZ32, ZZ32, String), (String, String),
(*) (String, String, String) and (Character, Character, String), plus deny at
(*) the same shapes that need the negative direction.
(*)
(*) The vararg form assert(x, y, failMsg: Any...) is deliberately not exercised
(*) and not declared: a vararg parameter does not typecheck against a call whose
(*) arguments need a coercion, so the four programs that write
(*) assert(3, o.foo(), "msg ", o.foo(), " instead of 3.") stay blocked and are
(*) a later rung.
(*)
(*) Both directions are pinned.  Every assert here is given equal arguments and
(*) every deny unequal ones, so a run that prints PASS shows the comparison was
(*) made and came out right; the values are freshly computed rather than
(*) written twice, so an identity comparison on boxed values would not pass.

  subC.verify()
  assert(cat[2], 'b')
  assert(subC[0], 'b')
  assert(subC[1], 'c')
  assert(subC[2], 'd')
  assert(subC[3], 'e')
  shouldRaise⟦IndexOutOfBounds⟦ZZ32⟧⟧ (fn() ⇒ subC[4])
end

  e = EmptyString
  assert(e.asFlatString, "", "EmptyString.javaString")
  c = CatString("abcd", "efgh")
  c.verify

end

(* The string library's flat, concatenated, sub- and empty strings, called under walk through the declarations the compiled checker could not type, with the values they answer. *)
component StringPieces
import String.{...}
import FlatString.{...}
export Executable

piecesOf(g: Generator[\(ZZ32, String)\]): String = do
    s: String := ""
    for (o, p) <- seq(g) do s := s || o || ":" || p || ";" end
    s
end

run() = do
    a = "a"^20
    b = "bcdefghijklmnopqrstu"
    cs = a || b
    flat = "abc"
    assert(cs.ilkName, "CatString", "two twenty-character strings concatenate into a CatString")
    sub = cs[18#5]
    assert(sub.ilkName, "SubString", "five characters across the two halves of a CatString are a SubString")

    assert(piecesOf(cs.splitWithOffsets()), "0:" || a || ";20:" || b || ";", "a concatenated string splits into its two halves at offsets 0 and 20")
    assert(piecesOf(sub.splitWithOffsets()), "0:aa;2:bcd;", "a substring across the halves splits into its part of each half")
    assert(cs[0], 'a', "the first character of the concatenated string is a")
    assert(cs[|cs| - 1], 'u', "the last character of the concatenated string is u")

    assert(flat.get(1), 'b', "get at 1 of abc is b")
    assert(cs.get(25), 'g', "get at 25 of the concatenated string is g")
    assert(sub.get(2), 'b', "get at 2 of the substring aabcd is b")
    assert(sub[4], 'd', "the substring aabcd indexed at 4 is d")
    assert(|sub|, 5, "the substring has five characters")
    assert(sub.asFlatString, "aabcd", "the substring flattens to aabcd")
    assert(sub[1#3], "abc", "three characters of the substring from 1 are abc")
    assert(sub CMP "aabcd", EqualTo, "the substring compares equal to aabcd")
    assert(sub CMP "aabce", LessThan, "the substring compares less than aabce")
    assert(sub CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP "AABCD", EqualTo, "the substring compares equal to AABCD ignoring case")
    assert('b' IN sub, true, "b is in the substring")
    assert('z' IN sub, false, "z is not in the substring")
    assert(sub.balanced(), "aabcd", "the substring balanced is aabcd")

    assert(flat[1:], "bc", "abc from 1 is bc")
    assert(flat[3:], "", "abc from 3 is empty")
    assert(flat[#2], "ab", "the first two characters of abc are ab")
    assert(flat[0#0], "", "zero characters of abc are empty")
    shouldRaise[\IndexOutOfBounds[\ZZ32\]\](fn () => flat[2#5])
    assert("abcdef"[2#3], "cde", "three characters of abcdef from 2 are cde")
    assert("abcdef".javaSubstr(2), "cdef", "the Java substring of abcdef from 2 is cdef")

    assert(reverse("abc"), "cba", "abc reversed is cba")
    assert(reverse(""), "", "the empty string reversed is empty")
    assert(reverse(cs), b.reverse.asString || a, "the concatenated string reversed is its second half reversed then its first")

    assert(flat.asDebugString, "J3/0:abc", "a flat string's debug form")
    assert(cs.asDebugString, "BC40/1:" || newline || spaces(8) || "J20/0:" || a || newline || spaces(8) || "J20/0:" || b, "a concatenated string's debug form indents its halves by eight")
    assert(EmptyString.asDebugString, "E0/0", "the empty string's debug form")

    assert(flatConcat("ab", "cd"), "abcd", "flatConcat of ab and cd is abcd")
    assert(flatConcat("ab", 'c'), "abc", "flatConcat of ab and c is abc")
    small = "ab" || CatString("cd", "ef")
    assert(small, "abcdef", "a short flat string and a short concatenated string concatenate to abcdef")
    assert(small.ilkName, "FlatString", "a short concatenation is flattened")
    assert(newline, lineSeparator, "newline is the line separator")

    assert(cs.stats().asString, "size = 40; depth = 1; maxFlat = 20; minFlat = 20; avFlat = 20.0; numFlat = 2", "the statistics of the concatenated string")
    assert(sub.stats().asString, "size = 5; depth = 1; maxFlat = 20; minFlat = 20; avFlat = 2.5; numFlat = 2", "the statistics of the substring count its base's flat pieces")
    assert(flat.stats().asString, "size = 3; depth = 0; maxFlat = 3; minFlat = 3; avFlat = 3.0; numFlat = 1", "the statistics of a flat string")

    var subs: String := EmptyString
    for i <- seq(1#40) do subs := CatString(subs, sub) end
    assert(subs.isBalanced, false, "forty substrings concatenated one by one are unbalanced")
    rebalanced = subs.balanced()
    assert(rebalanced.depth, 12, "forty substrings rebalanced have depth 12")
    assert(rebalanced, subs, "rebalancing keeps the characters")
    var pairs: String := EmptyString
    for i <- seq(1#40) do pairs := CatString(pairs, "xy") end
    rebalancedPairs = pairs.balanced()
    assert(rebalancedPairs.depth, 2, "forty two-character strings rebalanced have depth 2")
    assert(|rebalancedPairs|, 80, "forty two-character strings rebalanced have eighty characters")

    assert(EmptyString[0#0], "", "the empty string indexed by an empty range is empty")
    assert(EmptyString.bounds.asString, "[]", "the empty string's bounds are the empty range")
    shouldRaise[\IndexOutOfBounds[\ZZ32\]\](fn () => EmptyString.get(0))
    println("pieces " cs " " sub)
    println("PASS")
end

end
